title: The Night Before Our $2 Million Wedding, I Discovered My Billionaire Fiancé Was Using Me—So I Disappeared Before the Ceremony. But His Grandfather’s Secret Changed Everything.

blocks.text: I never imagined that the night before my wedding would become the night I discovered my entire relationship had been a lie.
My name is Ava Mitchell, and for eighteen months, I believed I was the luckiest woman alive.
Ethan Drake was handsome, wealthy, charming, and the heir to Drake Capital, one of the most powerful investment firms in New York.
His family owned skyscrapers, luxury hotels, private investment companies, and properties scattered across three continents.
When he proposed, he gave me an eight-carat diamond ring and promised that I would never have to worry about anything again.
Not because I needed his money. I had grown up comfortably, built my own career, and never dreamed of marrying into a billionaire family.
I believed him because, for the first time in my life, I thought someone loved me without expecting anything in return.
Our wedding was supposed to cost nearly $2 million.
Five hundred guests had been invited to the Grand Monroe Hotel. White roses covered the ballroom, a famous orchestra had been hired, and society magazines had already arranged exclusive photographs.
Or so I thought. The conversation that destroyed my wedding At approximately 10:40 p.m., I left the bridal lounge to retrieve my phone charger.
As I approached the private sitting room, I heard Ethan laughing.
“Are you absolutely sure she won’t discover anything?”
She was also supposed to be one of the special guests at our wedding.
I stopped outside the slightly open door.
“Ava is temporary. Once I get my grandfather’s shares, I’ll divorce her and marry you.”
“And what if she refuses to sign the divorce papers?”
“She won’t have a choice. The marriage agreement protects me. Besides, she trusts me completely.”
“Still can’t believe you’re going through with this, man.”
“My grandfather’s trust releases another five percent of Drake Capital’s voting shares once I satisfy the marriage requirement. I’ve done everything necessary. After tomorrow, those shares are mine.”
“It’s an investment. Two million dollars is nothing compared with what I’ll gain.”
Eighteen months of believing his promises, meeting his family, planning our future, and imagining children who would carry his last name.
Then Brooke asked the question that changed everything.
“What if your grandfather finds out about us?”
“He won’t. He’s old, and he barely understands what’s happening around him anymore.”
My eyes were burning, but I refused to cry.
Instead, I returned to my suite, locked it, and stared at the diamond ring on my finger.
A beautiful symbol of a marriage that had never been real.
Then I picked up my phone and called someone I hadn’t spoken to in almost three months.
“Yes,” I whispered. “Let’s proceed.” The secret agreement There was something Ethan didn’t know.
His grandfather, Richard Drake, had contacted me six months earlier.
At first, I assumed he simply wanted to get to know the woman his grandson intended to marry.
But during our second meeting, he asked me something unexpected.
I didn’t understand what he meant until he placed a folder on the table.
Inside were financial documents, private correspondence, and records showing that Ethan had been secretly manipulating company investments.
Richard explained that he had become suspicious of his grandson’s behavior.
He believed Ethan was rushing into marriage because of a clause in the family trust.
The clause required Ethan to marry someone his grandfather considered genuinely independent and trustworthy before receiving additional voting shares.
Richard had been looking for someone who could protect the company from being controlled by the wrong person.
He had apparently investigated me before Ethan proposed.

He knew I had worked in corporate restructuring, that I had refused several lucrative offers to conceal financial irregularities, and that I had once reported misconduct at a company even though doing so cost me my position.
But I didn’t understand why Richard was telling me all this.
Then he asked me to help him investigate Ethan.
I loved Ethan, and I didn’t want to believe the accusations.
He simply said, “If I’m wrong, you lose nothing. But if I’m right, you deserve to know before you marry him.”
Over the following months, I quietly helped Richard examine several suspicious transactions.
And eventually, we uncovered something disturbing.
Ethan wasn’t simply trying to inherit more shares.
He was preparing to transfer company assets through a network of shell companies, using his anticipated voting power to conceal the transactions.
Richard had already begun preparing legal measures to protect Drake Capital.
And now, after overhearing Ethan’s conversation, I finally had it. The bride who disappeared At 2:15 a.m., I packed a small suitcase.
I left my wedding dress hanging in the closet.
I removed every piece of jewelry Ethan had given me and placed them in their original boxes.
“Ethan, you wanted a temporary bride. Consider your wish granted.”
I handed the note to the hotel manager and asked him to deliver it personally.
Then I walked through the service entrance.
By 6 a.m., I was in a private residence outside Manhattan.
For the first time, I noticed how tired he looked.
“I hoped I was wrong about him,” he whispered.
